questions.question:
Consider the reaction given below:

\(\mathrm{C}_4 \mathrm{H}_{10}+\frac{13}{2} \mathrm{O}_2 \rightarrow 4 \mathrm{CO}_2+5 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\)

If \(\mathrm{174 ~g}\) of butane reacts with \(\mathrm{320~ g}\) of \(\mathrm{O_2,}\) the volume of \(\mathrm{H_2O}\) formed in ml is:
(Density of \(\mathrm{H_2O}\) is \(\mathrm{1 g/ml)}\))
1.1202.125
3.1384.145
questions.explanation:
Hint: Check stoichiometric ratio to find limiting reagent. Explanation: \(\begin{aligned} \mathrm{C}_4 \mathrm{H}_{10} {(\mathrm{g})} & +\quad \frac{13}{2} \mathrm{O}_{2_{(\mathrm{g})}} \longrightarrow 4 \mathrm{CO}_{2_{(\mathrm{g})}}+5 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}(\ell) \\ \mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{C}_4 \mathrm{H}_{10}} & =\frac{174}{58}=3 \quad \mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{O}_2}=\frac{320}{32}=10 \end{aligned} \) Stoichiometric ratio \(\frac{3}{1} \quad \frac{10}{\frac{13}{2}}=\frac{20}{13}=1.53\) L.R. \(\frac{13}{2} \mathrm{~mol} \mathrm{O}_2\) produces moles of \(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}=5\) \(1 \mathrm{~mol} \mathrm{O} \mathrm{O}_2\) produces moles of \(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}=\frac{5}{13 / 2}=\frac{10}{13}\) \(10 \mathrm{~mol} \mathrm{O} \mathrm{O}_2\) produces moles of \(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}=\frac{10}{13} \times 10=\frac{100}{13}\) Mass of \(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\) produced \(=\frac{100}{13} \times 18=138.46 \approx 138\) Volume of \(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\) produced\(=138 \times 1 \mathrm{ml}\) \(=138~ \mathrm{ml}\)

(2) Complete conjugation: All atoms in the ring are part of a continuous π-system (sp² or sp hybridization). (3) Hückel’s rule: Contains 4n+2 π-electrons (n=0,1,2,....). (4) Planarity: The ring must be flat to allow maximum π-orbital overlap. The cyclopentadienyl anion (q) is a planar, cyclic molecule with five carbon atoms and a negative charge, resulting in a total of six π-electrons, which is why it's aromatic. (II) Antiaromatic compounds are destabilized and highly reactive due to cyclic conjugation with 4n π-electrons. All the other conditions are similar to the aromatic ring. If we look at this cyclopropenyl anion (p), it obeys all conditions except Huckel's rule, and it obeys 4 n π electrons, and hence it belongs to the category of the anti-aromatic compound. Cyclooctatetraene (r) is not planar; instead, it adopts a "tub-shaped" conformation to minimize strain and avoid the destabilizing effects of antiaromaticity. It is a non-aromatic compound. So, the correct order of stability is given as follows: q > r > p. Hence, option 1 is the correct answer.

questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles And Techniques
questions.question:
Which of the following statements is incorrect?
1.Glycerol is purified by vacuum distillation.
2.Aniline is purified by steam distillation.
3.Chloroform and aniline can be separated by distillation.
4.Ethanol and water form an azeotropic mixture that can be separated by distillation.
questions.explanation:
Hint: In an azeotrope, no further separation can occur through distillation. Explanation: (1) Glycerol has a high boiling point and decomposes before reaching its normal boiling point at atmospheric pressure. Vacuum distillation reduces the pressure, thereby lowering the boiling point and allowing purification without decomposition. (2) Aniline is sparingly soluble in water and steam volatile. Steam distillation is suitable for purifying liquids that are immiscible with water and volatile in steam, allowing them to be distilled at a lower temperature than their normal boiling point. (3) Chloroform and aniline have different boiling points (chloroform: ~61°C, aniline: ~184°C). Therefore, they can be separated by fractional distillation. (4) Azeotropic mixtures are mixtures of liquids that boil at a constant temperature and have the same composition in the vapor phase as in the liquid phase. This means they cannot be completely separated by simple distillation because their boiling points are effectively the same at the azeotropic point. Ethanol and water are an azeotropic mixture that can’t be separated by distillation. To separate them further, methods like azeotropic distillation (using a third component), extractive distillation, or molecular sieves are required. Hence, option 4 is the correct answer.
